title: Cardinal Billing Account Reinstatement Terms by Pay Plan
content:
After a cancellation for nonpayment, the reinstatement terms of a Cardinal Billing Account depend on its pay plan.

| Pay plan | Reinstatement window (calendar days after the cancellation effective date) | Without-lapse period (calendar days) | Signed no-loss statement required for a reinstatement with a lapse | Reinstatement fee | Most reinstatements in one term |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Cardinal Direct Bill Monthly Plan | 15 | 0 (never without lapse) | Yes | $30.00 | 1 |
| Cardinal Card Autopay Monthly Plan | 20 | 3 | Yes | $25.00 | 1 |
| Cardinal EFT Autopay Monthly Plan | 20 | 3 | Yes | $25.00 | 1 |
| Cardinal Three-Pay Plan | 30 | 5 | Yes | $25.00 | 2 |
| Cardinal Two-Pay Plan | 30 | 5 | Yes | $20.00 | 2 |
| Cardinal Paid-in-Full Plan | 30 | 5 | Yes | $20.00 | 2 |

## Notes

- The window is the number of calendar days after the cancellation effective date within which reinstatement is available.
- The without-lapse period is the number of calendar days after the cancellation effective date within which a reinstatement payment restores coverage with no lapse; on the Cardinal Direct Bill Monthly Plan it is 0, so a reinstatement on that plan always carries a lapse.
- Every plan requires the named insured's signed statement of no loss for a reinstatement with a lapse.
- The fee is charged on each reinstatement.

Hypothetical comparison: a reinstatement payment posted 4 calendar days after the cancellation effective date falls within the without-lapse period on the Cardinal Three-Pay Plan (5 days) but not on the Cardinal Card Autopay Monthly Plan (3 days).
